zh.question: 星云为什么可见，出生质量怎样改变恒星的一生与遗骸？
zh.observe: 先比较成星云的发射、反射和遮挡，再转动行星状星云与超新星遗迹的壳层，找出物质来源和照明机制。沿同一中心拖动云、盘、主序和遗骸；对照 0.2、1、15、30 个太阳质量的代表分支。用独立半径标尺比较大小，用颜色与寿命理解主序差别，再把相伴恒星的示意轨道与数值三体实验分清。

academic.title: 先辨物质与光，再看恒星如何诞生
academic.body: 星云是气体和尘埃的云，不是一种固定年龄的天体。成星区的冷分子气体含少量尘埃；致密云核可能在引力下收缩，而气压、湍流与磁场提供支撑。角动量使落入物质形成盘，吸积与收缩可先于稳定氢聚变发光，部分年轻星体产生双极外流；大质量恒星的吸积与核心聚变可重叠。可见发射星云主要靠气体被电离后产生谱线等过程发光；反射星云的尘埃散射附近星光；暗云吸收和散射背景光。三种机制可在一个区域并存，不是三个必然先后阶段。行星状星云则是晚期恒星抛层，被露出的热核心照亮；它不是行星，也不是一次超新星。超新星遗迹的抛射物与被扫过的星际气体受冲击等过程影响，射电、可见光和 X 射线可能呈现不同结构。壳边看起来亮可来自更长视线路径，不能据二维圆环断定真实空间是一只平环。这里的 3D 是可逆教学形态，不是流体或辐射转移求解，也不重建某个实测星云。

academic.title: 质量、温度、寿命与遗骸是不同的问题
academic.body: 主序星靠核心氢聚变持续供能；在主序范围内，较大质量通常意味着更高温、更高光度和更短寿命。有效温度关系 L=4πR²σT⁴ 说明巨星即使表面较冷，也可因面积大而非常明亮；观测通量还取决于距离与消光。代表性低质量红矮星可活万亿年，远超过现今宇宙约 138 亿年的年龄；页面 0.2 个太阳质量的后三站是理论远未来，不强行安排太阳式红巨星、明亮行星状星云或超新星。太阳型示例经膨胀和抛层留下靠余热冷却的白矮星，不再靠稳定核心核聚变发光。15 与 30 个太阳质量示例分别选择中子星与黑洞分支，质量损失、组成、双星作用和坍缩条件也会改变结局，这些不是精确门槛。超新星外部遗迹与中心遗骸应分清；Ia 型涉及白矮星热核爆发，通常不留下中子星。部分中子星的发射束扫过地球才表现为脉冲，不能给所有中子星预设可见灯塔。黑洞的吸积盘需外部供气。太阳的表面耀斑来自磁能释放，不是核心聚变或持续太阳风的同义词。

academic.title: 行星可绕双星，也可绕其中一颗
academic.body: Kepler-47 中有三颗已确认行星绕两颗恒星的共同质心；另一种宽双星结构可让行星绕其中一颗，KOI-5 则有行星绕层级三星中的 A 星。画面保留成员与绕行关系，但轨道距离压缩、恒星大小放大，不重建观测轨道，也不证明长期稳定。另设的数值实验以三个固定的等质量数学案例按牛顿引力逐步积分三个平面点质量，使用固定步长 velocity-Verlet，和前述真实系统不是同一轨道。选 L₀、M₀ 后，T₀=√(L₀³/GM₀)，数值 G=1；播放时持续计算，步长0.001 T₀，历史窗口保留最近20 T₀。八字初值来自 Montgomery 作者页面，等边对照满足 ω²=1/√3；不规则游走的初值是本项目从等边起点稍作改变并筛选出的数值例子，没有随机力。轨迹线交叉可能发生在不同时刻，放大的星盘不能证明真实接触；本积分没有恒星半径、潮汐或碰撞模型，近遇无法解析或能量误差将超过0.1%便停止。微扰的位置差不证明混沌或长期稳定。

zh.misconception: 不是每个星云都在形成恒星，不是每颗恒星都以超新星结束。红矮星和白矮星的“矮”不是同一种供能机制；白矮星靠余热发光，中子星不一定被看成脉冲星。蓝白主序星通常更热，红巨星的大半径不代表质量同比变大；交叉轨迹也不证明相撞。
zh.boundary: 演化年龄和半径为近似教学锚点，0.2 个太阳质量的远未来从未在当前宇宙被完整观测。3D 云、盘、恒星、壳层和遗骸分别放大，不共用长度尺；颜色增强、形状可转动并不等于实测重建。独立比较镜头的成熟太阳型轮廓与行星轨道共用线性比例，但固定轨道不预测地球命运。体积明暗来自说明性密度的近似视线积分，不是实测亮度；没有求解外抛速度、冲击、真实电离、辐射传输或质量损失。星面颗粒与暗斑增强对比，致密遗骸不套用太阳颗粒。镜头近看恒星、拉远显示云壳，物质坐标与过程进度保持不变。双星/层级三星是构造；独立三体章才直接积分牛顿点质量，不含恒星尺寸、碰撞、潮汐、相对论或演化。避免直视真实太阳。

narration.label: 为什么看见一片云
narration.text: 宇宙里的云主要是气体，夹有尘埃。有些气体受到恒星的紫外光照射会发光；有些尘埃把星光散射给我们；还有些云遮住背后的光，看起来反而很暗。较密的云核可能收缩，物质经盘落向年轻的中心。中心先因收缩和吸积发亮，持续的核心氢聚变开启主序。
narration.cue: 比较成星云的三种照明，再把演化拖到云核、盘和主序，转动观察盘与两极外流。

narration.label: 不同的质量，不同的终点
narration.text: 小红矮星用燃料很慢，可以活到远远超过今天宇宙的年龄。它的最后几站还是理论推算。太阳型恒星会膨胀、抛出外层，留下靠余热发光的白矮星。大质量恒星的一种结局是核心坍缩超新星：外壳向外，致密遗骸留在中心。这里的例子留下中子星，但不是每颗恒星都爆炸，也不是每颗中子星都能看成闪烁灯塔。
narration.cue: 对照四条质量路径；在太阳型与15太阳质量结尾打开3D壳层，区分白矮星、中子星与外抛气体；查看低质量未来限定。

narration.label: 颜色、大小和光从哪里来
narration.text: 蓝白色主序星通常比橙红色主序星更热。可是一颗膨胀的红巨星，也能因为表面积很大而非常明亮。大小、质量和温度是三件不同的事。太阳日常的光热主要来自核心聚变；黑子、耀斑和太阳风则涉及表面与外层的不同过程。漂亮的星云照片还要看望远镜选了哪些波段。
narration.cue: 在类型比较里对照红矮星、太阳、红巨星和蓝白主序星，再切太阳结构与星云说明，辨认温度、半径、供能和观测波段。

narration.label: 一起绕行
narration.text: 行星不一定只绕一颗孤单的太阳。Kepler-47 的三颗行星绕一对双星；有的行星只绕双星中的一颗；KOI-5 的行星则绕三星中的 A 星。再看三种固定的等质量数学起点：八字、等边旋转和不规则游走。它们都逐步计算引力，却不是这些真实系统的轨道；游走也不是随机力在推动。轨迹交叉不等于恒星已经相撞。
narration.cue: 依次切换三个完整系统，指出每颗行星绕谁；再在三体数值章对比八字、等边与游走，并打开微扰叠加观察差异。

en.question: Why are nebulae visible, and how does birth mass change a star’s life and remnant?
en.observe: Compare emission, reflection and obscuration in one cloud geometry, then rotate planetary-nebula and supernova-remnant shells to identify matter and light sources. Scrub a cloud, disk, main-sequence star and remnant around the same center. Compare representative 0.2, 1, 15 and 30 solar-mass branches. Use a separate radius ruler for size, color and lifetime for main-sequence differences, and distinguish illustrative companion paths from the numerical three-body experiment.

academic.title: Identify matter and light before following star formation
academic.body: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust, not one fixed age of object. Cold molecular gas contains a little dust; dense cores may contract under gravity while pressure, turbulence and magnetic fields provide support. Angular momentum produces a disk, contraction and accretion can shine before sustained hydrogen fusion, and some young sources launch bipolar outflows. Massive stars can fuse while still accreting. Emission regions shine through ionization, recombination and related line processes; reflection nebulae scatter nearby starlight; dark clouds remove background light by absorption and scattering. These mechanisms can coexist and are not three inevitable stages. Planetary nebulae instead contain late stellar ejecta illuminated by an exposed hot core; they are neither planets nor supernovae. Supernova remnants contain ejecta and swept-up interstellar material affected by shocks and other processes. Radio, optical and X-ray views may show different structures. A bright shell rim can arise from a longer emitting sightline, not a flat ring. The reversible 3D teaching geometries are neither fluid or radiative-transfer solutions nor reconstructions of observed nebulae.

academic.title: Mass, temperature, lifetime and remnant answer different questions
academic.body: Main-sequence stars are sustained by core hydrogen fusion. Within the main sequence, greater mass generally means higher temperature, luminosity and a shorter lifetime. The effective-temperature relation L=4πR²σT⁴ explains how a cooler giant can still be very luminous through its large area; observed flux also depends on distance and extinction. Representative low-mass red dwarfs can last trillions of years, far beyond the present Universe’s age of about 13.8 billion years. The final three 0.2-solar-mass stops are a theoretical distant future, without an imposed Sun-like red giant, bright planetary nebula or supernova. The Sun-like example expands, sheds its envelope and leaves a white dwarf cooling through stored heat, without sustained core nuclear fusion. The 15- and 30-solar-mass examples select neutron-star and black-hole outcomes; mass loss, composition, binary interaction and collapse details also matter, so these are not fixed thresholds. Extended supernova debris and a compact central remnant are distinct. Type Ia involves thermonuclear disruption of a white dwarf and usually leaves no neutron star. Some neutron stars are detected as pulsars when emission beams sweep Earth; a visible lighthouse is not assigned to every one. A black-hole disk requires a matter supply. Solar flares release magnetic energy, distinct from core fusion and continuing solar wind.

academic.title: Planets can orbit a pair or just one star
academic.body: Kepler-47 has three confirmed planets orbiting the barycenter of its two stars. A sufficiently wide binary can allow a planet around one component, while KOI-5 has a planet around star A in a hierarchical triple. The scenes retain membership and orbit hierarchy but compress drawn separations and enlarge star markers; they neither fit observed orbits nor prove stability. The separate numerical experiment integrates three fixed equal-mass mathematical cases, not the observed systems, as three planar point masses under Newtonian gravity using fixed-step velocity-Verlet. Choosing L₀ and M₀ sets T₀=√(L₀³/GM₀), so numerical G=1. Playback uses step0.001 T₀ and keeps the latest20 T₀. Figure-eight initial conditions come from Montgomery’s author page; the equilateral comparison has ω²=1/√3. The wandering case is a project-screened departure from the equilateral start, with no random force. Trail crossings can occur at different times, and enlarged markers cannot establish contact. With no stellar radii, tides or collision physics, the integration stops at unresolved approaches or before proposed energy error exceeds0.1%. Finite-time perturbation differences prove neither chaos nor long-term stability.

en.misconception: Not every nebula forms stars, and not every star ends as a supernova. Red dwarfs and white dwarfs have different energy sources: a white dwarf glows through stored heat, and not every neutron star is seen as a pulsar. Blue-white main-sequence stars are generally hotter; a giant’s large radius does not imply proportionally greater mass. Crossing trails do not prove a collision.
en.boundary: Ages and radii are approximate teaching anchors, and the 0.2-solar-mass distant future has never been observed through a complete life in the present Universe. The 3D cloud, disk, star, shell and remnant are separately magnified with no shared length ruler; enhanced color and rotatable shape are not observed reconstructions. The mature Sun-like outline and planetary orbits share a linear scale only in the separate comparison view; fixed orbits do not predict Earth’s fate. Volume shading integrates an illustrative density along sightlines; it is not measured intensity. Ejecta speeds, shocks, physical ionization, radiation transfer and mass loss are not solved. Photospheric granules and dark regions have enhanced contrast; compact remnants are not given solar granulation. Camera close-ups of stars and wider cloud/shell views preserve matter coordinates and process progress. Binary and hierarchical-triple paths are constructions; only the separate three-body chapter integrates Newtonian point masses, excluding stellar sizes, collisions, tides, relativity and evolution. Never look directly at the Sun.

narration.label: Why a cloud becomes visible
narration.text: A space cloud is mostly gas with some dust. Gas can glow when a star’s ultraviolet light ionizes it. Dust can scatter starlight toward us, or block the light behind it and look dark. Dense cloud cores may contract as material falls through a disk toward a young center. Contraction and accretion shine first; sustained core hydrogen fusion begins the main sequence.
narration.cue: Compare three cloud illuminations, then scrub the evolution through dense core, disk and main sequence; rotate to distinguish the disk and polar outflows.

narration.label: Different masses, different endings
narration.text: A small red dwarf uses fuel slowly and can live far beyond today’s age of the Universe. Its last stops are theoretical predictions. A Sun-like star expands, sheds its envelope and leaves a white dwarf glowing through stored heat. One massive-star outcome is a core-collapse supernova: a shell moves outward while a compact remnant remains. This example leaves a neutron star, but not every star explodes, and not every neutron star is seen as a flashing lighthouse.
narration.cue: Compare all four mass paths. Open the final Sun-like and 15-solar-mass 3D shells to distinguish white dwarf, neutron star and outer gas; read the low-mass distant-future qualification.

narration.label: Color, size and the source of light
narration.text: Blue-white main-sequence stars are generally hotter than orange-red ones. An expanded red giant can still shine brightly because of its huge surface area. Size, mass and temperature answer different questions. The Sun’s ordinary light and heat come mainly from core fusion; spots, flares and solar wind involve different surface and atmospheric processes. A colorful nebula image also depends on which wavelengths a telescope observes.
narration.cue: Compare red dwarf, Sun, red giant and blue-white main-sequence star, then inspect solar structure and nebula notes to distinguish temperature, radius, energy and wavelength.

narration.label: Orbiting together
narration.text: A planet need not orbit a lone Sun. Kepler-47's three planets circle a stellar pair; another planet can circle just one star in a binary; KOI-5's planet circles A in a triple. Then compare three fixed equal-mass mathematical starts: a figure eight, rotating triangle and wandering path. Gravity is integrated step by step; none reproduces those observed systems, and the wandering is not driven by random forces. Crossing trails do not establish a collision.
narration.cue: Switch among all three complete systems and name each planet's host; then compare the figure eight, triangle and wandering case with the perturbation overlay.
